passages.text: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist; he has risen from the dead! That is why miraculous powers are at work in him.”
passages.sermon:
Herod was the tetrarch.
At that time, Herod heard reports about Jesus.
Herod spoke to his servants.
Herod said, “This man is John the Baptist.
John has risen from the dead.
That is why miraculous powers work in him.”
passages.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἤκουσεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὴν ἀκοὴν Ἰησοῦ καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτιστής αὐτὸς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αἱ δυνάμεις ἐνεργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτῷ

passages.text: Now Herod had arrested John and bound him and put him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, because John had been telling him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
passages.sermon:
Herod was the ruler called tetrarch.
Herod arrested John.
Herod tied John up.
Herod put John in prison.
Herod did this because of Herodias.
Herodias was the wife of Philip.
Philip was Herod’s brother.
John had been speaking to Herod.
John said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
passages.original: Ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης κρατήσας τὸν Ἰωάνην ἔδησεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ ἀπέθετο διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης αὐτῷ Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν αὐτήν

passages.text: Although Herod wanted to kill John, he was afraid of the people, because they regarded John as a prophet.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the ruler at that time.
Herod wanted to kill John.
Herod feared the people.
The people regarded John as a prophet.
passages.original: καὶ θέλων αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἐφοβήθη τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ὡς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον

passages.text: On Herod’s birthday, however, the daughter of Herodias danced before them and pleased Herod so much that he promised with an oath to give to her whatever she asked.
passages.sermon:
Herod was a ruler.
Herod had a birthday celebration.
Herodias was the wife of Herod’s brother Philip.
Herodias had a daughter.
Herodias’s daughter danced in front of the guests at Herod’s birthday.
Herod watched the dance.
Herod was very pleased by her dance.
Herod made a promise to her.
Herod swore an oath.
Herod promised to give her whatever she asked.
passages.original: Γενεσίοις δὲ γενομένοις τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ὠρχήσατο ἡ θυγάτηρ τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ καὶ ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ ὅθεν μεθ’ ὅρκου ὡμολόγησεν αὐτῇ δοῦναι ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσηται

passages.text: Prompted by her mother, she said, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”
passages.sermon:
Herodias was the mother of the girl.
The girl was Herodias’s daughter.
Herodias told her daughter what to ask for.
The girl listened to her mother.
The girl spoke to Herod.
She said, “Give me the head of John the Baptist.”
She wanted the head on a platter.
She asked for it to be given to her here.
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ προβιβασθεῖσα ὑπὸ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς Δός μοι φησίν Ὧδε ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ

passages.text: The king was grieved, but because of his oaths and his guests, he ordered that her wish be granted and sent to have John beheaded in the prison.
passages.sermon:
Herod was the king.
Herod felt sad.
Herod had made oaths.
Herod had guests with him.
Herod wanted to keep his oaths.
Herod wanted to please his guests.
Herod gave the order to grant the girl's request.
Herod sent men to the prison.
They beheaded John in the prison.
passages.original: Καὶ λυπηθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς συνανακειμένους ἐκέλευσεν δοθῆναι καὶ πέμψας ἀπεκεφάλισεν τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ

passages.text: John’s head was brought in on a platter and presented to the girl, who carried it to her mother.
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
\r\nThe king ordered John to be beheaded.
\r\nA man brought John’s head on a platter.
\r\nHe gave the platter to the girl.
\r\nThe girl took the platter to her mother.
passages.original: Καὶ ἠνέχθη ἡ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἐδόθη τῷ κορασίῳ καὶ ἤνεγκεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς

passages.text: Then John’s disciples came and took his body and buried it. And they went and informed Jesus.
passages.sermon:
John was a prophet.
\r\nHerod had John beheaded in prison.
\r\nJohn’s disciples came to the prison.
\r\nThey took John’s body.
\r\nThey buried John’s body.
\r\nJohn’s disciples went to Jesus.
\r\nThey told Jesus what had happened.
passages.original: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτόν καὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: When Jesus heard about John, He withdrew by boat privately to a solitary place. But the crowds found out about it and followed Him on foot from the towns.
passages.sermon:
Jesus heard about John’s death.
Jesus left that place.
Jesus went away by boat.
Jesus wanted to be alone.
He went to a quiet, empty place.
Many people heard where Jesus went.
Crowds came after Jesus.
They walked from the towns to find Him.
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν ἐν πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατ’ ἰδίαν καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πεζῇ ἀπὸ τῶν πόλεων

passages.text: When He stepped ashore and saw a large crowd, He had compassion on them and healed their sick.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stepped ashore.
He saw a large crowd.
Jesus felt compassion for the people.
He healed their sick.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν τοὺς ἀρρώστους αὐτῶν

passages.text: When evening came, the disciples came to Him and said, “This is a desolate place, and the hour is already late. Dismiss the crowds so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in a remote place with His disciples and a large crowd.
Evening came.
The disciples came to Jesus.
They spoke to Him.
They said, “This place is deserted.
It is already late.
Send the crowds away.
Let them go to the villages.
There they can buy food for themselves.”
passages.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἡ ὥρα ἤδη παρῆλθεν ἀπόλυσον οὖν τοὺς ὄχλους ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὰς κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς βρώματα

passages.text: “They do not need to go away,” Jesus replied. “You give them something to eat.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “They do not need to go away.”\r\nHe said, “You give them something to eat.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν ἀπελθεῖν δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν

passages.text: “We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
The disciples spoke to Jesus.
They said what they had.
They said, “We have only five loaves of bread here.
We also have two fish.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Οὐκ ἔχομεν ὧδε εἰ μὴ πέντε ἄρτους καὶ δύο ἰχθύας

passages.text: “Bring them here to Me,” Jesus said.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “Bring them here to Me.”
He meant the five loaves and the two fish.
Jesus wanted the food brought to Him.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Φέρετέ μοι ὧδε αὐτούς

passages.text: And He directed the crowds to sit down on the grass. Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven, He spoke a blessing. Then He broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was present with a large crowd.
He told the people to sit down on the grass.
Jesus took five loaves of bread and two fish.
He looked up to heaven.
Jesus spoke a blessing.
He broke the loaves.
Jesus gave the bread to His disciples.
The disciples gave the bread to the people.
passages.original: καὶ κελεύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνακλιθῆναι ἐπὶ τοῦ χόρτου λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἔδωκεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις

passages.text: They all ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.
passages.sermon:
Jesus fed a large crowd.
Everyone ate.
Everyone had enough food.
No one was hungry.
The disciples collected the leftover pieces.
They filled twelve baskets with the leftovers.
passages.original: Καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν καὶ ἦραν τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων δώδεκα κοφίνους πλήρεις

passages.text: About five thousand men were fed, in addition to women and children.
passages.sermon:
Jesus fed a large crowd.
He gave food to about five thousand men.
This number does not include the women.
This number does not include the children.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ πεντακισχίλιοι χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων

passages.text: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to the other side, while He dismissed the crowds.
passages.sermon:
Jesus acted immediately.
He told His disciples to get into the boat.
He told them to go ahead of Him to the other side of the lake.
Jesus stayed behind to dismiss the crowds.
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθέως ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πέραν ἕως οὗ ἀπολύσῃ τοὺς ὄχλους

passages.text: After He had sent them away, He went up on the mountain by Himself to pray. When evening came, He was there alone, but the boat was already far from land, buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sent the crowds away.
He went up on the mountain.
He went alone to pray.
Evening came.
Jesus was there by Himself.
The boat was already far from the land.
Waves battered the boat.
The wind was against the boat.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατ’ ἰδίαν προσεύξασθαι ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης μόνος ἦν ἐκεῖ τὸ δὲ πλοῖον ἤδη σταδίους πολλοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀπεῖχεν βασανιζόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων ἦν γὰρ ἐναντίος ὁ ἄνεμος

passages.text: During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went out to them, walking on the sea.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
He has power over nature.
It was night.
The night was divided into four watches.
The fourth watch was very late, before dawn.
During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went to His disciples.
The disciples were in a boat on the sea.
Jesus walked on the sea to reach them.
passages.original: Τετάρτῃ δὲ φυλακῇ τῆς νυκτὸς ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν

passages.text: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea, they were terrified. “It’s a ghost!” they said, and cried out in fear.
passages.sermon:
The disciples saw Jesus.
Jesus was walking on the sea.
The disciples became terrified.
The disciples said, “It is a ghost!”
The disciples cried out because they were afraid.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἐταράχθησαν λέγοντες ὅτι Φάντασμά ἐστιν καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου ἔκραξαν

passages.text: But Jesus spoke up at once: “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus saw His disciples were afraid.
Jesus spoke to them immediately.
Jesus said, “Take courage.”
Jesus said, “It is I.”
Jesus said, “Do not be afraid.”
passages.original: Εὐθὺς δὲ ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς αὐτοῖς λέγων Θαρσεῖτε ἐγώ εἰμι μὴ φοβεῖσθε

passages.text: “Lord, if it is You,” Peter replied, “command me to come to You on the water.”
passages.sermon: Peter was a disciple of Jesus.\r\nPeter spoke to Jesus.\r\nPeter said, “Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You on the water.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν Κύριε εἰ σὺ εἶ κέλευσόν με ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα

passages.text: “Come,” said Jesus. Then Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came toward Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus said, “Come.”
Peter left the boat.
Peter walked on the water.
Peter came toward Jesus.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἐλθέ Καὶ καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου ὁ Πέτρος περιεπάτησεν ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα καὶ ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: But when he saw the strength of the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink, cried out, “Lord, save me!”
passages.sermon:
Peter was a disciple of Jesus.
Peter walked on the water toward Jesus.
Peter saw that the wind was strong.
Peter became afraid.
Peter began to sink.
Peter cried out.
Peter said, “Lord, save me!”
passages.original: βλέπων δὲ τὸν ἄνεμον ἰσχυρὸν ἐφοβήθη καὶ ἀρξάμενος καταποντίζεσθαι ἔκραξεν λέγων Κύριε σῶσόν με

passages.text: Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter. “You of little faith,” He said, “why did you doubt?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was with Peter on the water.
Peter began to sink.
Immediately, Jesus reached out His hand.
Jesus took hold of Peter.
Jesus spoke to Peter.
Jesus said, “You have little faith.”
Jesus asked, “Why did you doubt?”
passages.original: Εὐθέως δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ὀλιγόπιστε εἰς τί ἐδίστασας

passages.text: And when they had climbed back into the boat, the wind died down.
passages.sermon: Jesus and Peter climbed into the boat.\r\nThe wind stopped.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναβάντων αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος

passages.text: Then those who were in the boat worshiped Him, saying, “Truly You are the Son of God!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in the boat with His disciples.
The disciples were in the boat with Him.
The disciples worshiped Jesus.
They said to Jesus, “Truly, You are the Son of God.”
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες Ἀληθῶς Θεοῦ Υἱὸς εἶ

passages.text: When they had crossed over, they landed at Gennesaret.
passages.sermon: Jesus and His disciples crossed the lake.\r\nThey reached the land at Gennesaret.
passages.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν εἰς Γεννησαρέτ

passages.text: And when the men of that place recognized Jesus, they sent word to all the surrounding region. People brought all the sick to Him and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak. And all who touched Him were healed.
passages.sermon:
The men of that place saw Jesus.
They recognized Him.
They sent word to all the surrounding region.
People heard the news.
They brought all the sick to Jesus.
They begged Jesus to let the sick touch the fringe of His cloak.
Everyone who touched His cloak was healed.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου ἀπέστειλαν εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον ἐκείνην καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μόνον ἅψωνται τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ καὶ ὅσοι ἥψαντο διεσώθησαν
